note: What to scan to keep the hypotheses alive, and how. `last_scanned` null = never. Add the world's communities, channels and forums here; a world may also hold them in an a2kay research note (see the sync step). A refresh reads `steps` in order.

sources.name: YouTube monetization policies (inauthentic / repetitive content)
sources.how_to_scan: Fetch the page; diff the 'Generic or Repetitive Content' section against platform_rules.json quotes; update `fetched`; open any new wording as a rule.

sources.name: YouTube Help: Shorts length and upload
sources.how_to_scan: Fetch; check max length and aspect rules against contracts/formats.json.

sources.name: Trade press on YouTube policy changes (socialmediatoday, ppc.land)
sources.how_to_scan: Search the site for 'YouTube' policy news since last_scanned; add each claim as evidence (stance for/against) to the matching hypothesis with the article URL and date.

sources.name: Own channel YouTube Studio analytics
sources.how_to_scan: 48-72 h after each upload read viewed-vs-swiped, retention 3 s / 10 s / end, avg view %. Record results with `experiments.py result`; never re-judge a hook before then.

sources.name: Creator communities (forums, Discord, Telegram, Reddit): the world's own list
sources.how_to_scan: Add one source row per community here with its URL. Scan for reports of demonetisation, template flags and format experiments with numbers; each report is one evidence entry with the post URL, date and author as attribution.

steps.do: List due sources: `hypotheses.py refresh WORLD` (cadence_days since last_scanned).
Scan each due source as its `how_to_scan` says; collect claims with date, URL, attribution.
Attach each claim: `hypotheses.py add-evidence`, or `add` for a new hypothesis. Evidence is never removed.
Re-evaluate: `hypotheses.py promote --all` applies the lifecycle rule; read what moved.
Mark the source: `hypotheses.py scanned WORLD SOURCE_ID`.
Policy: if a platform rule changed, edit platform_rules.json and run `policy.py check`.

Optional, when the a2kay MCP is available: sync with research/youtube-algorithm-research-optimization (hypotheses, log); `hypotheses.py export` writes the flat copy, `import` reads one back. a2kay is a backend, never required.
